key_insight: Particle trapping in a time-periodic vortex breaks down through a saddle-node bifurcation when inertia-driven outward drift overwhelms inward thermophoretic migration.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a tunable control threshold for predicting and preventing particle retention or loss in thermally driven microfluidic and aerosol transport systems.
method: Derived a small-Stokes-number reduced model for slow, cycle-averaged radial particle motion.
Analyzed fixed points and phase portraits to locate stable trapping states and separatrices.
Varied the dimensionless control parameter Π to show coalescence and disappearance of equilibria at the transition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phase portraits, bifurcation diagrams, and local asymptotic analysis, plus additional tests with different velocity and temperature profiles to verify robustness.
watch_item: The reduced model is asymptotic and cycle-averaged, so its predictions may weaken outside the small-Stokes-number regime or when the flow/temperature field departs strongly from the assumed profiles.
paper_title: Trapping-loss transition via a saddle-node bifurcation in thermophoretic particle transport driven by a time-periodic vortex
